title: Wipro Launches Dedicated Databricks Practice to Scale Enterprise AI
excerpt: The Indian IT giant sets up a new business practice integrating Databricks capabilities with its AI platforms, targeting industry-specific data modernization and AI deployment.
body:
• Wipro has launched a dedicated Databricks business practice to help enterprises modernize data infrastructure and deploy AI at scale.
  • The partnership integrates Databricks' agentic AI, data modernization, and analytics capabilities with Wipro's AI platforms including Wipro Intelligence™ and WEGA.
  • The practice builds on 300+ delivered use cases across banking, healthcare, telecom, manufacturing, and energy sectors.
  • Industry-specific solutions will target wealth management, manufacturing resilience, telecom transformation, and CFO operations.

Wipro has deepened its partnership with Databricks by establishing a self-contained business practice focused on helping enterprises modernize their data foundations and accelerate AI adoption. The move marks a significant step in the Indian IT services giant's push to position itself at the center of enterprise AI transformation.

A Dedicated Practice for Data and AI

The new Databricks business practice will integrate Databricks' capabilities in agentic AI, data modernization, application development, and analytics with Wipro Intelligence™, the company's suite of AI-powered platforms and services. The practice will also leverage Wipro's agent-native delivery platform, WEGA, to help clients transition from legacy systems to scalable, AI-ready data architectures.

A key component of the partnership is Databricks Genie, an AI-powered assistant that enables both business and technical users to interact with enterprise data using natural language. The tool is designed to help organizations generate insights faster by lowering the barrier to data access.

"Our long-standing collaboration with Databricks reflects a shared commitment to help enterprises move from AI experimentation to measurable value."

— Kanwar Singh, Managing Partner – Technology Services, Wipro

Industry Solutions Across Sectors

The practice builds on Wipro's track record of delivering more than 300 agentic AI and data use cases across industries including banking and financial services, healthcare, telecom, manufacturing, and energy. The collaboration has already earned recognition, with Wipro receiving Databricks' 2025 Banking Partner of the Year Award and the 2026 Innovation Partner of the Year Award.

Going forward, Wipro and Databricks will focus on developing AI-led solutions for several targeted areas: end-to-end wealth management and portfolio optimization in financial services, planning resilience for manufacturing and consumer goods, agentic AI-driven sales and marketing transformation for telecoms, and asset visibility and performance improvement for energy companies. The partnership will also pursue agentic AI-led CFO transformation by reimagining financial planning and analysis processes.

Enterprise AI at Scale

The partnership addresses a core challenge facing large enterprises: the gap between AI experimentation and production-scale deployment. Many organizations have built isolated AI pilots but struggle to connect them to governed, enterprise-wide implementations. Wipro's dedicated practice aims to bridge that gap by combining platform expertise with deep industry knowledge.

"This global practice with Wipro will enable enterprises to build trusted data foundations and deploy production-ready AI at scale, turning data intelligence into real, measurable business impact."

— Kori O'Brien, Senior Vice President, Partnerships, Databricks

What This Means for Indian Tech

For Wipro, the enhanced Databricks partnership reinforces its strategy of moving beyond traditional IT services into higher-value AI consulting and implementation. The company has been investing in AI capabilities across its portfolio, including recent initiatives around Anthropic's Claude and its own AI platforms. The dedicated practice model — with more than 1,500 engineers and consultants focused on Databricks — signals a broader industry trend where Indian IT services firms are building specialized AI practices to capture growing enterprise demand.

The partnership is designed to help joint customers become what both companies describe as "intelligent enterprises" — organizations that are secure by design, resilient by default, and ready for the next wave of technological reinvention.
